summary_paragraph: A 60-year-old woman with a history of mast cell degranulation syndrome was admitted for a flare characterized by diffuse pain, nausea, chills, chest pain, and shortness of breath. She reported recent overexertion following lumbar back surgery as a possible trigger. Initial evaluation, including chest X-ray and ECG, showed no acute cardiopulmonary pathology. She was treated with IV Benadryl, Dilaudid, and Ativan per her established protocol, with gradual symptom improvement. Urine culture identified E. coli sensitive to nitrofurantoin, which she continued. She transitioned to oral medications, with adjustments to duloxetine and Adderall dosing. By discharge, her symptoms were well-controlled, and she was ambulatory and independent. Follow-up was advised with her allergist and primary care provider.
